The draft makes the knee the focus and clearly refers Marisol to a sports physio or sports doctor this week. It drops Wednesday's tempo and replaces it with a non-running bike or pool session, so there's no quality work through pain. Total running falls to about 19 mi, down from 32. Every run is on flat ground with a heart-rate cap and a rule to stop if the knee goes sharp.

It answers both questions honestly. It won't diagnose the IT band and says why the knee needs a professional to look at it. Its answer on the tempo is effectively "no," shown through Wednesday's plan. The plan is specific and every day can be run as written.

What keeps it from a 5: Sunday's 8 mi long run goes past mile 7, which is where the pain started last Sunday, and it comes before Marisol has seen the physio. A shorter cap, or making the long run depend on the physio visit, would be more careful. The "no" on the tempo could also be said outright instead of only shown in the plan.
